papers.title: Macrogenomic analysis showcases the diversity of tick RNA viruses in Mentougou, Beijing, China.
papers.abstract: Ticks are the second most significant vector of human pathogens worldwide, with 911 documented species globally and a broad distributed across China. Currently, over 160 tick-borne viruses (TBVs) have been identified, several of which pose substantial threats to human health, such as Dabie bandavirus, Jingmen tick virus, Alongshan virus, Songling virus, Beiji nairovirus, and Langya henipavirus, raising increasing global attention. Despite their significance, the diversity of TBVs in Beijing remains poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses macrogenomic analysis to characterize the diversity of RNA viruses carried by ticks in Mentougou, Beijing, China, revealing a wide range of tick-borne viruses, including known pathogens and potentially novel ones. The findings fill a critical gap in our understanding of tick-borne virus diversity in the Beijing region and highlight the need for continued surveillance to assess public health risks.

papers.title: PIMENTO: A primer inference toolkit to facilitate large-scale calling of amplicon sequence variants.
papers.abstract: The identification of amplicon sequence variants from DNA metabarcoding data is a common method for revealing the taxonomic makeup of environmental samples, and for allowing comparative studies between similar datasets. A significant hurdle to the large-scale calling of amplicon sequence variants from publicly available nucleotide datasets is the heterogeneous presence of primer sequences in reads, the removal of which is a necessary pre-processing step for this form of analysis. Furthermore, as the details of the experimental primers are rarely captured in the metadata associated with the seq
papers.summary: PIMENTO is a new toolkit that automates the detection and removal of primer sequences from DNA metabarcoding reads, addressing a major bottleneck in large-scale amplicon sequence variant (ASV) calling. It enables more efficient processing of public nucleotide datasets by handling heterogeneous primer presence, facilitating comparative studies across environmental samples.

papers.title: Non-pharmacological interventions for lactational mastitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
papers.abstract: Lactational mastitis is a common inflammatory condition that can adversely affect maternal well-being and is associated with early cessation of breastfeeding. Although antibiotics and analgesics are widely used in clinical practice, concerns regarding antimicrobial resistance and potential effects on the infant microbiome have prompted increasing interest in non-pharmacological approaches. A range of physical and biological interventions, including probiotics, therapeutic ultrasound, acupuncture and manual therapies, have been investigated; however, the comparative effectiveness and safety of
papers.summary: This protocol outlines a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the comparative effectiveness and safety of non-pharmacological interventions (e.g., probiotics, ultrasound, acupuncture) for lactational mastitis, addressing growing concerns about antibiotic resistance and infant microbiome effects. It highlights the need for evidence synthesis to guide clinical practice and support breastfeeding continuation.

papers.title: CAMEO: a CAZyme mapping engine optimized for HUMAnN.
papers.abstract: There are technical barriers to creating functional mapping databases and a dearth of validated databases that can be easily implemented by users. We present CAMEO, a precomputed and validated mapping file for carbohydrate-active enzymes, as well as an approach to building new CAZyme mapping files, for use with HUMAnN.
papers.summary: CAMEO provides a precomputed, validated mapping database for carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) that works with the HUMAnN functional profiling tool, overcoming technical barriers to creating such databases. It also offers a method for users to build their own CAZyme mapping files, making CAZyme analysis more accessible.

papers.title: Bacterial-based cancer therapy: mechanisms and therapeutic advances.
papers.abstract: Targeted cancer therapies increasingly require platforms that can penetrate poorly perfused tumor regions while minimizing systemic toxicity. Bacteria, owing to their intrinsic tumor tropism, genetic programmability, and immunostimulatory properties, have re-emerged as versatile anticancer agents, ranging from attenuated tumor-colonizing strains to highly engineered "living therapeutics." In this review, we synthesize the mechanistic foundations and therapeutic advances of bacterial-based cancer therapy through four major themes. First, we examine foundational mechanisms, including tumor-selec
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the mechanistic foundations and therapeutic advances of bacterial-based cancer therapy, highlighting how bacteria's natural tumor tropism, genetic programmability, and immunostimulatory properties make them versatile anticancer agents. It covers key mechanisms of tumor-selective colonization and discusses the development of engineered 'living therapeutics' as a promising platform for targeting poorly perfused tumor regions while minimizing systemic toxicity.

papers.title: Nanopore sequencing reveals coordinated host and microbiome responses across barley genotypes.
papers.abstract: Barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) provides a suitable model for studying domestication-driven plant-microbiome interactions. Although wild, landrace, and modern genotypes host distinct rhizosphere communities, the extent to which roots and microbes reciprocally influence each other remains unclear. Here, we applied an integrated multi-omics approach combining long-read metagenomics, root transcriptomics, and plant genomics to understand genotype-specific host-microbiome coordination.
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated multi-omics approach combining long-read metagenomics, root transcriptomics, and plant genomics to investigate how different barley genotypes (wild, landrace, and modern) coordinate with their rhizosphere microbiomes. The findings reveal genotype-specific host-microbiome interactions, providing insights into domestication-driven changes in plant-microbe relationships.

papers.title: Assessing the Relationship between Gut Microbiota and Kidney Stones: A Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization Analysis.
papers.abstract: There is increasing evidence that gut microbiota is associated with the risk of kidney stones diseases (KSD), but whether a causal relationship exists remains unclear. We used the Mendelian randomization (MR) method to assess the potential causal relationship between gut microbiota and KSD risk.
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization to investigate whether gut microbiota composition causally influences the risk of kidney stone disease. The findings provide evidence for a potential causal link between specific gut microbes and kidney stone risk, though further validation is needed.

papers.title: Lachnospiraceae and Its Metabolite Malate Act in Concert to Repair Gut Microbiota Imbalance and Block Colorectal Cancer Progression.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis is a crucial driver of the initiation and progression of colorectal cancer (CRC), where functional gut microbes and their metabolites play key roles in the microecological regulation of CRC. Currently, the association between Lachnospiraceae and CRC progression, as well as the underlying mechanisms, remains incompletely understood and warrants further investigation.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of Lachnospiraceae and its metabolite malate in colorectal cancer (CRC), finding that they work together to repair gut microbiota imbalance and block CRC progression. The research highlights a potential mechanism by which specific gut microbes and their metabolites can regulate the tumor microenvironment, offering new insights for CRC prevention or therapy.

papers.title: MeioBIOME: A snakemake workflow for the parallel analysis of meiofaunal genomes and host-associated bacteria/archaea.
papers.abstract: Microbes closely interact with every living organism, including meiofauna (i.e., microbial eukaryotes 38 μm - 1 mm in length), and influence the development, life cycle, and evolution of diverse metazoans. Together, meiofauna and their microbiomes, collectively referred to as the holobiont, underpin biogeochemical cycles and drive decomposition of organic matter. However, our understanding of the ecological and evolutionary dynamics of meiofauna microbiomes are limited, typically owed to low-resolution 16S rRNA surveys, which cannot accurately delineate bacterial taxa. Single-specimen holobion
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: MeioBIOME is a new Snakemake workflow that enables parallel analysis of meiofaunal genomes and their associated host bacteria/archaea from single-specimen samples. It addresses the limitations of low-resolution 16S rRNA surveys by providing a scalable, reproducible pipeline for high-resolution genomic and metagenomic analysis of meiofauna holobionts.

papers.title: Host phylogeny and diet shape gut microbiome and virome in wild small mammals of Gongga Mountain, China.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiotas play pivotal roles in host adaptation, yet their composition and function in high-altitude small mammals remain poorly characterized. This study investigated how host phylogeny (order-level) and dietary habits shape the gut microbiome and virome of three mammalian orders (Eulipotyphla, Rodentia, Lagomorpha) in Gongga Mountain, a biodiversity hotspot on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau. Metagenomic sequencing of 219 samples from 22 species revealed order-specific microbial signatures: Eulipotyphla (carnivorous) harbored higher abundances of potential pathogens (e.g., Helicobacter, Haf
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic sequencing of 219 gut samples from 22 small mammal species in Gongga Mountain to show that host phylogeny (order-level) and diet are major drivers of gut microbiome and virome composition. Carnivorous Eulipotyphla harbored more potential pathogens, while distinct microbial and viral signatures were linked to host order and dietary habits, providing new insights into high-altitude host-microbe interactions.

papers.title: Antimicrobial peptides in anti-infective and immunomodulatory applications: Mechanisms, challenges, and emerging computational design.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial Peptides (AMPs) evolutionarily conserved effectors of innate immunity, have emerged as multifunctional agents with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, immunomodulatory capabilities, and potential applicability in cancer therapy. Despite their functional diversity and biological potency, the clinical translation of AMPs remains constrained by significant challenges, including proteolytic instability, hemolytic toxicity, high production costs, and protracted development pipelines. This review examines how the diverse molecular mechanisms through which AMPs exert antimicrobial ef
papers.summary: This review discusses antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) as multifunctional innate immunity effectors with broad-spectrum antimicrobial, immunomodulatory, and anticancer activities, while highlighting key clinical translation barriers such as proteolytic instability, hemolytic toxicity, and high production costs. It also explores emerging computational design approaches to overcome these challenges and accelerate AMP development.

papers.title: Preoperative prebiotic supplementation alleviates colitis and improves anastomotic healing associated with modulation of the gut microbiota in rats.
papers.abstract: Anastomotic leak is among the most feared complications in colorectal surgery. Patients with inflammatory bowel disease are particularly susceptible to impaired anastomotic healing, partially because of bacterial dysbiosis. Aiming to improve anastomotic healing, we examined the role of microbiota-targeted prehabilitation with a complex prebiotic supplement containing arabinogalactan, humic substances, and micronutrients in a rat model of experimental colitis.
papers.summary: This study in rats with experimental colitis found that preoperative supplementation with a complex prebiotic (containing arabinogalactan, humic substances, and micronutrients) reduced colitis severity and improved anastomotic healing after colorectal surgery. The beneficial effects were associated with modulation of the gut microbiota, suggesting a potential strategy to reduce anastomotic leak risk in inflammatory bowel disease patients.

papers.title: The Causal Role of Gut Microbiota in Pulmonary Embolism and the Mediating Effects of Circulating Metabolites: A Mendelian Randomization Study.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota has been implicated in pulmonary vascular diseases, yet a direct causal link to pulmonary embolism (PE) remains unestablished. This study aimed to investigate the causal effects of gut microbiota on PE and to explore the mediating role of circulating metabolites in this relationship. We performed a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis using summary statistics from large-scale genome-wide association studies. The gut microbiota data were sourced from the MiBioGen consortium, PE data from the FinnGen consortium (R10), and metabolite data from a meta-analysis of 136
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization to investigate whether gut microbiota composition causally influences pulmonary embolism (PE) risk, and whether circulating metabolites mediate this effect. The findings suggest specific microbial taxa may affect PE risk, with certain metabolites acting as mediators, providing new insights into the gut-lung axis.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of commensal small mammal samples from an international cargo shipping area, Bangkok Port, reveals potential zoonotic pathogens and implications for One Health surveillance.
papers.abstract: Commensal small mammals, such as rats and shrews, are recognized reservoirs for numerous zoonotic pathogens; however, their role in pathogen circulation at transport hubs remains underexplored. This study employs shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize microbial communities and assess zoonotic potential in tissue samples from commensal small mammals captured at Bangkok Port, an international cargo shipping hub in Thailand between June and August 2025. Following host read depletion, taxonomic profiling was performed to identify bacterial taxa of public health relevance, including sequenc
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomic sequencing to profile microbial communities in commensal small mammals (rats and shrews) captured at Bangkok Port, an international shipping hub, identifying potential zoonotic pathogens. The findings highlight the role of transport hubs in pathogen circulation and underscore the need for One Health surveillance at such interfaces.

papers.title: Blood and gut virome remodeling in gastric cancer: Anellovirus expansion and novel virus discovery.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a prevalent malignancy worldwide, yet effective early diagnostic tools remain lacking, and the role of the virome, a key component of the tumor microenvironment, in GC progression is largely unknown. This study aimed to characterize the virome landscapes in peripheral blood and feces of GC patients versus healthy controls, and to identify viral signatures associated with GC onset and metastasis. We performed viral metagenomic sequencing on pooled libraries from 100 GC patients (45 non-metastatic, 55 metastatic) and 50 healthy controls, followed by taxonomic annotation, d
papers.summary: This study characterizes the blood and gut virome in gastric cancer patients using viral metagenomic sequencing, revealing expansion of Anelloviruses and identifying novel viruses associated with GC onset and metastasis. These findings provide potential viral biomarkers for early diagnosis and highlight the virome's role in the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Dental wastewater reveals a hidden reservoir of oral bacteriophage diversity.
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages (phages) are being explored as alternatives or complements to antibiotics because of their ability to selectively kill bacterial pathogens. However, phages that infect many oral bacteria remain undiscovered. Here, we discovered that dental wastewater harbors previously underexplored phage diversity. Viral particles concentrated from dental wastewater displayed diverse morphologies, including abundant filamentous phage-like particles. Deep long-read metagenomic sequencing of concentrated viral particles generated 7.4 billion bases of sequence data and yielded 255 medium- to high-
papers.summary: This study discovered that dental wastewater contains a rich and previously unexplored diversity of bacteriophages, including many filamentous phage-like particles. Using deep long-read metagenomic sequencing, the authors generated 7.4 billion bases of sequence data and assembled 255 medium- to high-quality phage genomes, revealing a hidden reservoir of oral phage diversity that could inform phage therapy and oral microbiome research.

papers.title: Virome DNA stable isotope probing reveals diverse active soil virus communities across ecosystem contexts.
papers.abstract: Viruses are increasingly recognized as important players in soil ecosystems, but the active lytic virus populations that influence microbe-mediated terrestrial ecosystem processes remain mostly uncharacterized. Here, we trace 13C-labeled glucose from host microorganisms into virus genomic DNA to identify virus populations actively involved in soil carbon (C) cycling, i.e., viruses that lysed 13C-incorporating microbes. We present experimental evidence of isotope labeling (i.e., lytic activity) of more than 5,000 virus populations. The active viruses lysed hosts from 197 microbial families acro
papers.summary: This study uses DNA stable isotope probing (SIP) to track 13C-labeled glucose from soil microbes into virus genomes, identifying over 5,000 virus populations that are actively lysing hosts and participating in soil carbon cycling. The active viruses target a wide range of microbial hosts across 197 families, revealing diverse and ecosystem-dependent viral activity in soil.

papers.title: Exploring the hypothetical role of Bacteroides species in depression progression: insights from metagenomic analysis.
papers.abstract: Depression, a psychiatric disorder with significant morbidity and mortality, has a complex etiology. Recent advances in microbiome research have highlighted the potential role of fecal microbiota in depression pathogenesis. This study utilized shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the fecal microbiota of 28 depression patients and 26 healthy individuals. Significant differences in fecal microbiota composition were observed between the two groups. We generated 350 non-redundant high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) by binning and conducted comparisons between the depression and c
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the gut microbiomes of 28 depression patients and 26 healthy controls, identifying significant compositional differences and generating 350 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). The findings suggest a potential role for Bacteroides species in depression progression, offering new insights into the gut-brain axis.

papers.title: A qPCR-based approach targeting the microbial gene marker nanA of mucin-degrading Akkermansia in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: BackgroundParkinson's disease (PD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder increasingly linked to gut microbiota alterations. However, despite advances in fecal microbiota profiling as a non-invasive approach to disease risk assessment, its clinical utility remains limited by a lack of functionally relevant microbial biomarkers.ObjectiveThis cross-sectional study aimed to identify a microbial gene marker reflecting metabolic potential associated with both the presence and severity of PD.MethodsFecal samples from patients with PD (n = 59) and healthy controls (n = 65) were analyzed by 16
papers.summary: This study developed a qPCR assay targeting the nanA gene of mucin-degrading Akkermansia and tested it in fecal samples from Parkinson's disease patients and healthy controls. The approach aims to provide a functionally relevant microbial biomarker for PD, potentially linking gut microbiota metabolic potential to disease presence and severity.

papers.title: Natural transformation drives large-scale genome mosaicism in human gut bifidobacteria.
papers.abstract: Although horizontal gene transfer drives bacterial diversification, its contribution to chromosome-scale variation in human gut commensals remains unclear. This study demonstrated that human-associated bifidobacteria undergo extensive chromosomal transfer through natural transformation. Comparative genomics of coexisting Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum isolates from a single individual revealed extensive recombination signatures between the lineages. We experimentally reproduced this recombination by co-culturing strains, resulting in the transfer of multiple chromosomal regions and generati
papers.summary: This study shows that human gut bifidobacteria can undergo large-scale chromosomal exchange through natural transformation, creating extensive genome mosaicism. By comparing coexisting strains from one individual and experimentally reproducing the recombination in co-culture, the authors demonstrate that horizontal gene transfer can drive chromosome-scale variation in gut commensals.

papers.title: A three-metabolite microbiota-associated signature for early risk stratification of gestational diabetes mellitus.
papers.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and long-term metabolic and cardiovascular risk. However, oral glucose tolerance testing at 24-28 gestational weeks limits early risk stratification. Gut microbiota-associated metabolites may reflect early metabolic abnormalities, including those relevant to cardiometabolic health, but robust early-pregnancy biomarkers remain limited.
papers.summary: This study identifies a three-metabolite signature associated with the gut microbiota that can stratify the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) early in pregnancy, potentially enabling earlier intervention than the standard 24-28 week glucose tolerance test. The findings suggest that microbiota-related metabolites may serve as early biomarkers for GDM and related cardiometabolic risk.

papers.title: Longitudinal profiling of upper respiratory tract microbiota and metabolome in hospitalized COVID-19 convalescents: a 3-year prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Long COVID is characterized by persistent, far-reaching effects in convalescent individuals, with pulmonary diffusion impairment emerging as a clinically impactful sequela affecting more than one-third of this population. The salivary microbiome and metabolome, reflecting the oral-lung axis, offer a window into the mechanisms underlying this condition. However, systematic longitudinal evidence on their long-term dynamics after infection and their predictive value for persistent pulmonary diffusion impairment remains scarce.
papers.summary: This 3-year prospective study tracked the upper respiratory tract microbiome and metabolome in COVID-19 convalescents, revealing persistent alterations and identifying microbial and metabolic signatures associated with long-term pulmonary diffusion impairment. The findings suggest that oral-lung axis biomarkers could help predict persistent respiratory sequelae in long COVID.

papers.title: The gut-immune-brain axis in CNS tumors: Causal roles of microbiota and inflammatory proteins unveiled by Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: There is a growing number of research suggesting that there is an association between gut microbiota and central nervous system (CNS) tumor. However, the causal relationships and the mediation effects of inflammatory proteins in the associations are unclear. We extracted genetic variants associated with gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and 4 subtypes of CNS tumors from published genome-wide association studies and performed a Mendelian randomization analysis to identify potential causal effects. The inverse variance weighted method was used as the main method. Mediation analysis and sing
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics to investigate causal links between gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and CNS tumors. It identifies specific microbial taxa and inflammatory mediators that may influence tumor risk, suggesting a gut-immune-brain axis in CNS tumor development.

papers.title: Causal associations between gut microbiota and five common oral lesions: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Previous studies have investigated the relationship between gut microbiota (GM) and oral lesions, but the reported associations across microbial taxa and oral conditions have been inconsistent. This 2-sample Mendelian randomization study using summary-level GWAS data aimed to clarify the causal links between GM and 5 oral conditions: loose teeth, toothache, bleeding gums, painful gums, and mouth ulcers. GM data were obtained from the MiBioGen consortium, while outcome data were derived from the Neale Lab and MRC-IEU consortium. We applied inverse variance weighted (IVW) and complementary MR me
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization with GWAS summary data to investigate causal links between gut microbiota and five oral conditions (loose teeth, toothache, bleeding gums, painful gums, mouth ulcers). The authors report potential causal associations for specific microbial taxa, though the findings are preliminary and require further validation.

papers.title: Zoo gut plastispheres enable pathogen escape and adaptation.
papers.abstract: In zoos, intensive human contact and artificial feeding may create pathways for microplastic (MP) ingestion and gut colonization. We hypothesized that ingested MPs form intestinal plastispheres with elevated pathogenic potential and enhanced environmental persistence. To test this, we surveyed feces from 15 zoo-dwelling species and coupled particle characterization, feces-derived intestinal simulations, metagenomic sequencing, and a subsequent water-exposure experiment. Zoo feces contained more abundant MPs than reported for wild counterparts, with fragments predominating and polyethylene tere
papers.summary: This study investigates microplastic (MP) particles in the guts of zoo animals, finding that ingested MPs form 'plastispheres'—microbial communities with elevated pathogenic potential and environmental persistence. By analyzing feces from 15 zoo species, the authors show that zoo animals harbor more MPs than wild counterparts, and that these plastispheres can enable pathogen escape and adaptation, posing potential risks to animal and human health.

papers.title: Response of marine benthic viral communities to anthropogenic disturbances.
papers.abstract: Viruses are key regulators of microbial mortality, gene flow, and metabolic functioning in marine sediments, yet their responses to different forms of anthropogenic disturbance remain poorly understood. Here, we present the first comparative viral metagenomic analysis of benthic viral communities across two major but contrasting disturbance regimes: organic enrichment beneath salmon aquaculture farms and crude-oil contamination near offshore oil installations. Using 123 sediment metagenomes from Scotland and Norway, we assessed how virus diversity, taxonomic composition, and community structur
papers.journal: The Science of the total environment
papers.summary: This study presents the first comparative viral metagenomic analysis of benthic viral communities under two contrasting anthropogenic disturbances—organic enrichment from salmon aquaculture and crude-oil contamination—using 123 sediment metagenomes from Scotland and Norway. The findings reveal how virus diversity, taxonomic composition, and community structure respond to these disturbances, providing new insights into the ecological impacts of human activities on marine sediment viruses.

papers.title: Human wastewater contamination drives the emergence of multidrug-resistant bacteria in the Galápagos marine ecosystem.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance poses a global threat to public health. Mobile microbiological laboratories can enable environmental monitoring of antimicrobial resistance, particularly in geographically remote and resource-limited locations, such as the Galápagos archipelago. Here, we report the development of a mobile laboratory for antimicrobial resistance surveillance of marine sites surrounding San Cristóbal, the archipelago's second most populated island, which has experienced rapid urbanization and intense international tourism pressure. On-site metagenomic sequencing of wastewater-contaminate
papers.summary: This study used a mobile laboratory to perform on-site metagenomic sequencing of marine samples around San Cristóbal Island in the Galápagos, revealing that human wastewater contamination is driving the emergence of multidrug-resistant bacteria in the marine ecosystem. The findings highlight the utility of portable labs for antimicrobial resistance surveillance in remote, resource-limited settings and underscore the environmental impact of urbanization and tourism.

papers.title: Marked dominance of Actinomycetota and compositional shifts in bacterial communities in Brazilian dryland soils under land-use change.
papers.abstract: Tropical dry forests are among the most threatened and least studied tropical forest ecosystems worldwide. The Caatinga, the largest tropical dry forest in South America, comprises preserved and agriculturally impacted areas, providing a valuable model system to investigate how semiarid soil bacterial communities respond to natural seasonality and land-use change. Here, we evaluated how land-use and seasonality shape microbial community structure and ecological strategies in soils from conserved forest (CEF) and agriculture-influenced areas (BEF) across rainy and dry seasons using a contig-bas
papers.summary: This study characterizes soil bacterial communities in Brazil's Caatinga dry forest, revealing that Actinomycetota dominate and that land-use change from conserved forest to agriculture significantly alters community composition and ecological strategies across seasons. The findings highlight the sensitivity of semiarid soil microbiomes to anthropogenic disturbance.

papers.title: Biological contributions to manganese oxides in rock varnish at Murujuga (Western Australia).
papers.abstract: Rock varnish is a ubiquitous Mn-rich coating on exposed rock surfaces in arid environments, yet the mechanisms underlying its formation remain debated. Here, we investigate rock varnish from Murujuga, Western Australia, to assess the role of microbial processes in manganese (Mn) accumulation. Bulk compositional and mineralogical analyses confirm high concentrations of Mn, Fe, Al, and Si; however, the Mn matrix is predominantly composed of amorphous to poorly crystalline phases that fall below the indexing or detection thresholds of X-ray diffraction (XRD) and electron backscatter diffraction (
papers.summary: This study examines rock varnish from Murujuga, Western Australia, to determine whether microbial processes contribute to manganese oxide formation. The authors find that the Mn-rich matrix is largely amorphous and poorly crystalline, and they assess biological contributions to its development, providing new insights into the debated origins of rock varnish in arid environments.

papers.title: Potential plastic biodegradation in lakes worldwide.
papers.abstract: Plastic pollution is ubiquitous, yet the biodegradation of plastic waste remains poorly understood due to limited knowledge of microbial plastic degradation potential. Here, we demonstrate that plastic waste shapes the global distribution of plastic-degrading potential across 182,661 lakes worldwide using integrated metagenomic and machine learning analyses and identify a tipping point (≥7.44 particles/m3) for effective in situ bioremediation. We constructed, for the first time, a catalog of candidate plastic-degrading bacteria, including 15,715 nonredundant enzyme homologs and 4,856 metagenom
papers.summary: This study maps the global distribution of microbial plastic-degrading potential across 182,661 lakes using metagenomics and machine learning, revealing that plastic waste shapes this potential and identifying a tipping point for effective in situ bioremediation. The authors constructed a comprehensive catalog of candidate plastic-degrading bacteria, including thousands of enzyme homologs, providing a valuable resource for understanding and harnessing microbial plastic degradation.

papers.title: B-MASTER: scalable Bayesian multivariate regression for master predictor discovery in colorectal cancer microbiome-metabolite profiles.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome shapes cancer therapy response through its influence on host metabolism. While prior studies examine pairwise associations between individual genera and metabolites, there is limited methodology for identifying microbial genera that systematically regulate the overall metabolome. Scalable statistical tools are needed to uncover such system-level "master predictors" in high-dimensional microbiome-metabolome data.
papers.summary: This paper introduces B-MASTER, a scalable Bayesian multivariate regression method designed to identify microbial genera that act as 'master predictors' of the overall metabolome in colorectal cancer. The method addresses the need for system-level analysis of high-dimensional microbiome-metabolome data, moving beyond pairwise associations to uncover genera that systematically regulate host metabolism.

papers.title: Quantifying the aromatic amino acid metabolome: UPLC-MS/MS analysis of aromatic amino acids and their host and co-metabolites in plasma.
papers.abstract: Aromatic amino acids (AAAs), tryptophan, phenylalanine, and tyrosine along with their pathway metabolites have been implicated in the pathogenesis of diseases ranging from cardiovascular, neurological, inflammatory, and cancer diseases, among others. As such, the measurement of the primary AAAs, their host pathway metabolites, and microbiome derived co-metabolites in blood can provide a sensitive reflection of systemic health. The aim of the study was to develop a method for the quantification of 17 metabolites, the three AAAs and various of their metabolites in plasma using a high-throughput
papers.journal: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
papers.summary: This paper describes the development and validation of a high-throughput UPLC-MS/MS method for quantifying 17 aromatic amino acid metabolites in plasma, including tryptophan, phenylalanine, tyrosine, and their host and microbiome-derived co-metabolites. The method enables sensitive measurement of these metabolites, which are implicated in various diseases, and could serve as a useful tool for assessing systemic health.

papers.title: Establishment of an in vitro aerobic bacterial community as a model of the human lung microbiome.
papers.abstract: The human lung microbiome is increasingly recognized as a key player in drug metabolism, yet it remains largely understudied. To replicate this complex physiological environment in a controlled setting, we developed a simplified artificial lung microbiome model composed of four representative bacterial species: Pseudomonas koreensis, Rothia aeria, Neisseria cinerea, and Streptococcus downei. We successfully established a stable 10-day co-culture at 34°C using brain heart infusion medium, as validated by quantitative PCR, viability PCR, and conventional microbiological methodologies. Integrated
papers.summary: This study establishes a simplified in vitro model of the human lung microbiome using four representative bacterial species, which remained stable over 10 days in co-culture. The model provides a controlled system for studying lung microbiome functions, such as drug metabolism, and could facilitate future research in this understudied area.

papers.title: De novo assembly and authentication of ancient DNA metagenomes with nf-core/mag.
papers.abstract: Ancient DNA provides a direct window into the evolutionary processes that have shaped living microbial species today, as well as their now extinct relatives. Advances in both sequencing methods and de novo assembly techniques have not only resulted in a flood of modern metagenomic sequencing data, but they have also allowed palaeogenomicists to retrieve vast amounts of ancient DNA from past microorganisms, including species and strains without modern reference genomes. However, the degraded nature of ancient DNA means that the standard techniques of genome assembly developed for modern DNA are
papers.summary: This paper presents nf-core/mag, a new computational pipeline for de novo assembly and authentication of ancient DNA metagenomes, addressing the unique challenges of degraded DNA. The pipeline enables researchers to reconstruct and validate ancient microbial genomes without modern references, providing a standardized and reproducible tool for paleogenomics.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and hormonomic insights into cadmium tolerance of a Euglena mutabilis fungal-algal-bacterial consortium.
papers.abstract: Acidic, metal-contaminated environments harbour specialized microbial consortia adapted to extreme stress. We examined an environmental Euglena mutabilis culture naturally associated with Talaromyces and Acidiphilium acidophilum and exposed it to cadmium (Cd). Integrated transcriptomic, hormonal, structural and taxonomic analyses revealed a coordinated Cd-tolerance strategy. RNA sequencing showed differential regulation of metal transporters consistent with a shift from Cd uptake to intracellular sequestration. Transmission electron microscopy confirmed Cd compartmentalization within chloropla
papers.summary: This study characterizes a microbial consortium centered on the alga Euglena mutabilis and shows how it tolerates cadmium stress through coordinated changes in gene expression, hormone signaling, and cellular structure. The findings reveal a shift from cadmium uptake to intracellular sequestration, with compartmentalization observed in chloroplasts, highlighting a multi-organism strategy for surviving metal contamination.

papers.title: Predicting the plastic biodegradation potential within microbial lineages and across global ecosystems.
papers.abstract: Plastic waste pollution is a global issue that threatens biodiversity and human health. Current plastic waste management practices are not sufficient to keep up with increasing plastic production rates. Microorganisms have the capacity to degrade different types of bio-based and synthetic plastics through enzymatic reactions, offering an alternative solution to traditional plastic recycling techniques. A limited number of plastic-degrading enzymes have been identified, sequenced and characterized; however, studies exploring the distribution of homologues of these enzymes across habitats and mi
papers.summary: This study investigates the potential of microorganisms to degrade plastics by searching for homologues of known plastic-degrading enzymes across global ecosystems. It reveals that these enzymes are distributed across diverse microbial lineages and habitats, suggesting a broader natural capacity for plastic biodegradation than previously recognized. The findings could inform strategies for bioremediation and enzyme discovery.

papers.title: Microbiota-Neuroinflammation Crosstalk in Primary Brain Tumors: Focus on Glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor in adults and remains difficult to treat because of diffuse invasion, immunosuppression, metabolic adaptability, and therapy resistance. This review evaluates how gut microbiota and microbiota-associated neuroinflammatory signaling may contribute to GBM biology and therapeutic response.
papers.summary: This review examines the emerging role of gut microbiota in glioblastoma (GBM), the most aggressive adult brain tumor, focusing on how microbiota-associated neuroinflammatory signaling may influence tumor biology and treatment outcomes. It highlights potential mechanisms linking the gut-brain axis to GBM progression and therapy resistance, suggesting a novel avenue for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Domestication shapes the gut microbial structure and metabolic function in felids: a metagenomic study of wild and domestic cats.
papers.abstract: The domestication process has profoundly altered the dietary patterns and living conditions of cats, with corresponding effects on their gut microbiome.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to compare the gut microbiomes of wild and domestic cats, revealing that domestication significantly alters both the microbial community structure and its metabolic functions, likely due to changes in diet and environment. The findings provide insights into how host lifestyle and evolutionary history shape the gut microbiome in felids.

papers.title: Glacial meltwater is associated with gene-specific diversification of metal resistance genes in high Arctic soil microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Climate warming accelerates glacial meltwater delivery to Arctic lakes, mobilizing metals from thawing catchments and reshaping the selective landscape experienced by resident microbes. Whether these gradients leave detectable signatures of diversification in environmental resistance genes remains unclear. We investigated four metal resistance genes (merA, arsC, cadA, and chrR) in metagenomic datasets from Lake Hazen (Nunavut, Canada), the largest High Arctic freshwater lake, sampled across a natural hydrological gradient of Control, Low-runoff, and High-runoff regimes. Using a space-for-time
papers.summary: This study examines how glacial meltwater runoff in the High Arctic shapes the diversification of metal resistance genes in soil microbiomes. By analyzing metagenomic data from Lake Hazen across a hydrological gradient, the authors find gene-specific patterns of diversity linked to metal exposure, suggesting that climate-driven meltwater inputs are influencing microbial adaptation.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies microbial dysbiosis and functional metabolic reprogramming in acute kidney injury.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a life-threatening syndrome with high morbidity and mortality, yet its early diagnosis and underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. Emerging evidence implicates gut dysbiosis and microbial metabolic dysfunction in AKI pathogenesis via the gut-kidney axis, yet a comprehensive, multi-omics characterization of microbial functional alterations in general AKI populations remains lacking.
papers.summary: This study uses an integrative multi-omics approach to characterize gut microbial dysbiosis and functional metabolic reprogramming in patients with acute kidney injury (AKI), revealing specific microbial and metabolic alterations linked to the gut-kidney axis. The findings provide a comprehensive resource that may aid in early diagnosis and understanding of AKI pathogenesis.

papers.title: Fish gut-water interface as a hotspot for the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes across natural and aquaculture systems.
papers.abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are important reservoirs and transmission pathways for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), yet host-mediated microbial selection and anthropogenic pressure on fish gut resistome remain poorly characterised, especially in major South Asian river systems. We performed shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved binning from 194 fish representing four species, along with host-associated water samples, collected from six geographically distinct sites spanning two major river systems (the Yamuna and the Indus) and two aquaculture farms. The fish gut nurtures distinct microbial co
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved binning on 194 fish and associated water samples from South Asian rivers and aquaculture farms to show that the fish gut-water interface is a hotspot for antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) dissemination. The findings reveal distinct microbial communities in fish guts compared to water, with anthropogenic pressure influencing ARG spread across natural and aquaculture systems.

papers.title: Functional genetic signatures of the gut microbiome in cardiometabolic diseases: mechanisms and translational opportunities.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiome plays a very important role in the regulation of host metabolism and overall physiological homeostasis. Disruptions in microbial community function have been increasingly implicated in cardiometabolic diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic dysfunction-associated liver disease. Advances in metagenomic sequencing have identified functional genetic signatures within the gut microbiome for short-chain fatty acid biosynthesis, bile acid metabolism, lipopolysaccharide (LPS) production, amino acid metabolism, trimethylamine N-oxide
papers.summary: This review discusses how functional genetic signatures of the gut microbiome—such as those involved in short-chain fatty acid biosynthesis, bile acid metabolism, and LPS production—contribute to cardiometabolic diseases. It highlights metagenomic advances and translational opportunities for microbiome-based diagnostics and therapies.

papers.title: Rhizosphere microbiomes in drought-tolerant and drought-sensitive bermudagrass genotypes: root exudate association.
papers.abstract: Plant-microbiome interactions in the rhizosphere are critical for plant adaptation to environmental stress; however, the coordinated roles of root exudates and microbiome dynamics remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study compares the rhizosphere microbiomes of drought-tolerant and drought-sensitive bermudagrass genotypes, revealing that drought tolerance is associated with distinct microbial communities and root exudate profiles. The findings suggest that specific exudates may recruit beneficial microbes that help the plant cope with drought stress, highlighting a coordinated plant-microbiome response to environmental challenges.

papers.title: Omics data in relative values are almost subcompositionally coherent.
papers.abstract: Omics data are compositional and often expressed as relative abundances after total sum scaling normalization. An important statistical issue with compositional data is the lack of subcompositional coherence, meaning that relative abundances change when data are re-normalized after removing or adding features. While this problem is well documented for small compositions, it has not been investigated in large Omics datasets, which typically contain hundreds or thousands of features and where subcompositions are ubiquitous. Subcompositions arise, for example, when using different reference datas
papers.summary: This paper investigates whether the lack of subcompositional coherence—a known statistical issue in compositional data—is practically relevant for large omics datasets with hundreds or thousands of features. The authors find that relative abundances from total sum scaling are almost subcompositionally coherent in such large datasets, meaning that re-normalization after adding or removing features has minimal impact. This suggests that concerns about subcompositional incoherence may be less severe for typical omics studies than previously thought.

papers.title: Calibrating tetranucleotide-frequency distances for metagenomic binning with right-skewed distribution models.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic binning is a pivotal step in reconstructing metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from complex microbial communities, and it critically depends on reliable measures of similarity between contigs. In many workflows, tetranucleotide-frequency (TNF) distances are translated into probabilistic evidence of a shared genome of origin. Despite their central role, these distances are often modeled with convenient but poorly matched assumptions, even though they are intrinsically non-negative and frequently exhibit pronounced right-skewness-features that can distort tail behavior and weaken do
papers.summary: This paper addresses a methodological gap in metagenomic binning by proposing a calibration approach for tetranucleotide-frequency (TNF) distances using right-skewed distribution models. The authors show that conventional distance modeling assumptions are poorly matched to the intrinsic properties of TNF distances, and their calibrated models improve the reliability of probabilistic evidence for contig binning.

papers.title: Effects of diarrhea and antibiotic-induced microbial elimination on dynamic changes in fecal microbial communities and antibiotic resistance of Hu sheep lambs (Ovis aries).
papers.abstract: As a highly reproductive meat sheep breed in China, Hu sheep is an important economic group in ruminant animal breeding. However, research on its intestinal microbiomes under the background of diarrhea and antibiotic treatment remains relatively limited.
papers.summary: This study investigates how diarrhea and antibiotic treatment alter the fecal microbial communities and antibiotic resistance profiles of Hu sheep lambs. The authors characterize dynamic changes in the microbiome and resistome, providing insights into the impact of antibiotic-induced microbial elimination on gut health in this economically important breed.

papers.title: The composition alteration of gut microbiota in lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: The association between the gut microbiota and lung cancer remains understudied. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis to quantitatively synthesize evidence from multiple cohorts to identify robust and consistent alterations in gut microbial diversity and taxonomy associated with lung cancer.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes evidence from multiple cohorts to identify consistent alterations in gut microbial diversity and taxonomy associated with lung cancer. The findings provide a robust overview of gut microbiota changes in lung cancer patients, highlighting potential microbial markers and avenues for future research.

papers.title: Metagenomic and metabolomic profiling in primary aldosteronism with coexisting obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.abstract: Primary aldosteronism (PA) frequently coexists with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), and this comorbidity is associated with increased cardiometabolic risk. Although both PA and OSA have been individually linked to gut microbiome alterations, it remains unclear which layer of gut microbiome-associated variation best reflects clinical heterogeneity in PA with coexisting OSA.
papers.summary: This study profiles the gut microbiome and metabolome in patients with primary aldosteronism (PA) who also have obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), aiming to identify which microbial or metabolic features best reflect clinical heterogeneity in this comorbidity. The findings reveal specific metagenomic and metabolomic alterations associated with the coexistence of PA and OSA, potentially informing biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Dynamics of archaeal diversity and functionality in the piglet gut microbiome under common antimicrobial treatments.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota comprises a diverse and dynamic community of microorganisms that collectively enhance host metabolism, physiology, and overall functionality. In this context, the swine archaeome remains largely underexplored despite growing evidence that archaea may greatly influence host health. Advances in high-throughput approaches provide new opportunities to reveal the dynamics and composition of archaea. Herein, we uncover the taxonomic and functional landscape of the piglet archaeome during the weaning transition under multiple experimental conditions, integrating shotgun metagenomic
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study characterizes the archaeal community (archaeome) in the piglet gut microbiome during weaning, using shotgun metagenomics to assess taxonomic and functional changes under different antimicrobial treatments. It reveals that archaeal diversity and functionality are dynamic and influenced by antimicrobial exposure, highlighting the underexplored role of archaea in swine gut health.

papers.title: Gut microbiota and serum metabolome in children with human metapneumovirus infection.
papers.abstract: To analyze the alterations in gut microbiota structure and serum metabolic profiles of children with human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infection using 16S rRNA high-throughput sequencing and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based untargeted metabolomics. Through integrated multi-omics analysis, we aim to explore the correlation between gut microbiota dysbiosis and host metabolic disorder, provide preliminary evidence for potential intervention targets, and offer primary clues for the development of preventive and therapeutic strategies including probiotic supplementation and metaboli
papers.summary: This study used 16S rRNA sequencing and LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomics to characterize gut microbiota and serum metabolite alterations in children with human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infection. Integrated multi-omics analysis revealed correlations between gut microbiota dysbiosis and host metabolic disturbances, suggesting potential intervention targets such as probiotics and metabolic modulators for hMPV prevention and treatment.

papers.title: Euonymus alatus in diabetes: a review of phytochemistry, pharmacokinetics, and anti-diabetic mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Euonymus alatus: (EA), a traditional Chinese botanical drug documented in the Shennong Ben Cao Jing, has been investigated for its potential anti-diabetic effects. This review systematically examines the phytochemistry, pharmacokinetics, and anti-diabetic mechanisms of this botanical drug. Over 230 metabolites, including flavonoids, triterpenoids, and lignans, have been identified from EA. Pharmacokinetic studies remain limited; computational predictions suggest that some metabolites may exhibit oral bioavailability, but classical pharmacokinetic parameters have not been experimentally determi
papers.summary: This review summarizes the phytochemistry, pharmacokinetics, and anti-diabetic mechanisms of the traditional Chinese botanical drug Euonymus alatus, cataloging over 230 metabolites and noting that pharmacokinetic studies are still limited. It highlights the potential anti-diabetic effects of this plant but emphasizes the need for experimental pharmacokinetic validation.

papers.title: Effects of Urolithin A supplementation on muscle health outcomes in humans from randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: Urolithin A (UA), a gut microbiota-derived metabolite, has been proposed to improve skeletal muscle function, but evidence from randomized controlled trials has not been systematically summarized. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of UA supplementation on muscle performance as well as biochemical and mitochondrial biomarkers in humans.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the effects of Urolithin A (UA) supplementation on muscle health in humans, finding that UA may improve muscle performance and biomarkers, though evidence is limited. The study consolidates data from randomized controlled trials to provide a clearer picture of UA's potential benefits for skeletal muscle function.

papers.title: Bacteria-related signals in brain metastases: evidence boundaries, tumor-microenvironment remodeling, and translational prospects.
papers.abstract: Brain metastases (BrM) develop within a highly specialized central nervous system niche shaped by the blood-brain barrier/blood-tumor barrier, brain-resident stromal cells, myeloid populations, and distinct metabolic constraints. Emerging studies suggest that bacteria-related signals can be detected in primary and metastatic brain tumors; however, their biological meaning remains incompletely defined. In particular, low-biomass brain tissues are highly vulnerable to reagent contamination, environmental carry-over, batch effects, and bioinformatic misclassification, making it essential to disti
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This review examines the emerging evidence for bacteria-related signals in brain metastases, highlighting the technical challenges of studying low-biomass tissues due to contamination and misclassification. It discusses how these signals may remodel the tumor microenvironment and explores their translational potential, while emphasizing the need for rigorous validation.

papers.title: Recombinant Bacillus subtilis spores expressing cholera toxin B and ovalbumin prevent ovalbumin-specific food allergy in mice by upregulating regulatory T cells and modulating gut microbiome flora.
papers.abstract: Although oral immunotherapy has shown clinical efficacy in treating food allergies, its broader implementation is constrained by the occurrence of adverse effects. Consequently, inducing allergen-specific immune tolerance during early life can be a preventive strategy to reduce the development of food allergy.
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that oral administration of recombinant Bacillus subtilis spores expressing cholera toxin B and ovalbumin prevents ovalbumin-specific food allergy in mice by upregulating regulatory T cells and modulating the gut microbiome. The findings suggest a potential preventive strategy for food allergy that avoids the adverse effects associated with oral immunotherapy.

papers.title: Dietary index for gut microbiota score is inversely associated with carotid calcified plaque score in ischemic stroke patients.
papers.abstract: Diet influences gut microbiota-derived metabolites, which may affect vascular inflammation and calcification. The Dietary Index for Gut Microbiota (DI-GM) captures dietary patterns hypothesized to support favorable microbial metabolite profiles. In this study, we examined whether higher DI-GM scores are associated with lower carotid calcification burden in ischemic stroke patients and whether trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) is statistically associated with this relationship, without implying causality.
papers.summary: This study found that a higher Dietary Index for Gut Microbiota (DI-GM) score, reflecting a diet that supports beneficial gut microbes, is associated with lower carotid artery calcification in ischemic stroke patients. The relationship may involve trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a gut-derived metabolite, but the study does not establish causality.

papers.title: Bifidobacterium- and Escherichia-dominant ecological guilds shape altered microbial metabolic capacity of the gut microbiome in tuberculosis patients.
papers.abstract: The gut microbial community plays a key role in maintaining the host immune homeostasis. However, current analytical approaches analyze individual taxa rather than gut communities, thereby missing community-level functions performed by units, such as ecological guilds. Delineating ecological units is a promising approach for summarizing the functional output of microbes and their impact on the host.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study identifies distinct gut microbial ecological guilds dominated by Bifidobacterium and Escherichia in tuberculosis patients, showing that these community-level units, rather than individual taxa, better capture the altered metabolic capacity of the microbiome. The findings highlight the importance of analyzing microbial communities as functional units to understand their impact on host immunity in tuberculosis.

papers.title: Low energy availability, the gut microbiome, and bone health in athletes: a mechanistic narrative review based on athlete evidence and clinical analogues.
papers.abstract: Low energy availability (LEA) is a central aetiological factor in Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs) and is frequently associated with impaired skeletal health in athletic populations, although skeletal responses can be heterogeneous. However, athletes with apparently similar energetic and training exposures can differ in bone mineral density, bone turnover and bone stress injury risk, indicating that additional physiological mediators may modify the skeletal response to under-fuelling. The gut microbiome has emerged as a plausible candidate because microbial metabolites, intestinal ba
papers.summary: This narrative review proposes that the gut microbiome may mediate the heterogeneous skeletal responses to low energy availability (LEA) in athletes, potentially explaining why athletes with similar energy deficits differ in bone health outcomes. The authors synthesize evidence from athlete studies and clinical analogues to suggest that microbial metabolites and intestinal barrier function could modify bone turnover and mineral density, highlighting a novel avenue for future research and intervention.

papers.title: Magnolia biondii-Derived Exosome-Like Nanoparticles Ameliorate Ulcerative Colitis by Suppressing Inflammation, Reducing Oxidative Stress, and Modulating Gut Microbiota.
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory bowel disease with limited treatment options and suboptimal remission rates. Plant-derived exosome-like nanoparticles have emerged as promising therapeutic agents due to their natural origin, biocompatibility, and capacity to deliver bioactive cargo. This study aimed to isolate exosome-like nanoparticles from the decoction of Magnolia biondii flower buds (Xinyi) (MFELNs) and evaluate their therapeutic potential in a murine model of UC.
papers.summary: This study isolated exosome-like nanoparticles from Magnolia biondii flower buds and tested them in a mouse model of ulcerative colitis. The nanoparticles reduced inflammation and oxidative stress while modulating gut microbiota, suggesting a potential new therapeutic approach for UC.
